title: Italian for Work
shortDescription: Job-ready Italian for restaurants, hotels, care work, shops, warehouses, farms, building sites and delivery — plus your rights at work.
description:
A practical course for people who work, or want to work, in Italy. Each unit is a job track: finding a job and interviews, restaurants and kitchens, hotels and cleaning, care work, shops and supermarkets, warehouses and factories, farms, building sites, delivery — and a final unit on your contract, payslip, holidays and sick leave.

In every unit you learn the words of the job with pictures and audio, then practise a real workplace conversation out loud (an interview, taking an order, reporting a broken machine, calling in sick), and finish with a review and a printable study sheet.
objectives:
Read job adverts and handle a job interview
Use the words and instructions of your job
Talk to customers, colleagues and your manager
Understand safety signs and report problems or injuries
Understand your contract and payslip and know your rights

lessons.title: The job interview
lessons.summary: Answer the employer's questions about experience and availability.

blocks.title: The situation
blocks.body: You are at an interview for a job in a warehouse near Bologna. The manager asks you some questions.

blocks.title: Il colloquio di lavoro
blocks.caption: Manager

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.italian: Buongiorno, si accomodi. Come si chiama?
lines.english: Good morning, please sit down. What is your name?

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Good morning. My name is Ravi Kumar.

replies.english: Pleased to meet you, I'm Ravi Kumar.

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.english: Do you have experience in this job?

lines.speaker: You
lines.italian: Sì, ho lavorato due anni in un magazzino.
lines.english: Yes, I worked two years in a warehouse.

replies.english: A little, but I learn quickly.

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.italian: Può lavorare anche di notte e il sabato?
lines.english: Can you also work nights and on Saturdays?

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Yes, I'm available.

replies.italian: Il sabato sì, la notte no.
replies.english: Saturdays yes, nights no.

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.english: Do you have a residence permit?

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Yes, for employed work.

replies.english: Yes, here is a copy.

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.english: Good. Do you have a driving licence?

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Yes, a B licence.

replies.english: No, but I come by bus.

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.italian: Perfetto. Le facciamo sapere entro venerdì.
lines.english: Perfect. We will let you know by Friday.

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Thank you very much, goodbye.

replies.english: Thank you, have a nice day.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: In interviews always use **Lei** and say **Buongiorno** when you enter. Bring copies of your **permesso**, **codice fiscale** and ID.

blocks.title: The situation
blocks.body: You are a carer for Signora Rosa, 88. Her daughter Giulia calls in the evening to ask how her mother is.

blocks.title: Parlare con la famiglia
blocks.caption: Giulia (daughter)

lines.speaker: Giulia (daughter)
lines.italian: Ciao, sono Giulia. Come sta la mamma oggi?
lines.english: Hi, it's Giulia. How is mum today?

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Good evening Giulia. Today she's well.

replies.english: Today she's a bit tired.

lines.speaker: Giulia (daughter)
lines.english: Has she eaten?

lines.speaker: You
lines.italian: Sì, a pranzo ha mangiato la pasta e la frutta.
lines.english: Yes, at lunch she ate pasta and fruit.

replies.english: She ate little.

lines.speaker: Giulia (daughter)
lines.english: Has she taken her medicines?

lines.speaker: You
lines.italian: Sì, tutte, alle otto e alle venti.
lines.english: Yes, all of them, at eight and at eight pm.

replies.english: Yes, the blood-pressure tablet.

lines.speaker: Giulia (daughter)
lines.english: And her blood pressure?

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Blood pressure is normal: 130 over 80.

replies.english: A bit high, 150 over 90.

lines.speaker: Giulia (daughter)
lines.italian: Va bene. Domani viene il medico alle dieci.
lines.english: All right. Tomorrow the doctor comes at ten.

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Perfect, I'll wait for him. Good night!

replies.english: OK. See you tomorrow!

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: Write down the medicines, the times and the doctor's number on a sheet near the fridge. In an emergency call **112** first, then the family.

lines.italian: Buongiorno, corriere. Ho un pacco per Ferrari.

lessons.title: Calling in sick
lessons.summary: Call your boss to say you can't come to work.

blocks.title: The situation
blocks.body: You wake up with a high fever. You call your boss at 6:30, before your shift.

blocks.title: Avvisare che sei malato
blocks.caption: Boss

lines.speaker: Boss
lines.english: Hello?

lines.speaker: You
lines.italian: Buongiorno, sono Imran. Mi scusi, oggi non posso venire.
lines.english: Good morning, it's Imran. Sorry, I can't come in today.

replies.english: Good morning, it's Imran. I'm ill.

lines.speaker: Boss
lines.english: What happened?

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: I have a high fever.

replies.italian: Ho mal di schiena, non riesco a camminare.
replies.english: I have back pain, I can't walk.

lines.speaker: Boss
lines.english: I'm sorry. Are you going to the doctor?

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Yes, I'm going to the doctor this morning.

replies.english: Yes, I'm calling the doctor now.

lines.speaker: Boss
lines.italian: Va bene. Mandami il numero del certificato.
lines.english: OK. Send me the certificate number.

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Of course, I'll send it to you on WhatsApp.

replies.english: OK, as soon as I have it.

lines.speaker: Boss
lines.english: Rest. Get well soon!

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Thank you, goodbye.

replies.english: Thank you very much, see you soon.

items.italian: Non mi avete pagato gli straordinari.
